players.product: all-flash arrays / DirectFlash modules (hyperscaler design win)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO said the sudden rise in component costs forced the whole high-tech industry to raise prices, and that higher sales per unit plus customer pull-ins ahead of future price increases represented nearly a third of Q1 year-on-year revenue growth; the CEO said that without pricing or pull-ins the company is still growing well in the 20s, which he called a clear signal of share gains (win rates significantly higher over the last couple of quarters). Operating profit was $159 million (operating margin 15.1%), up over 90% year-over-year.
quarterly_data.figure: nearly a third of Q1 YoY revenue growth from pricing and pull-ins; operating profit $159 million, 15.1% operating margin

quarterly_data.signal: Guidance framing: the full-year guide implies 48% of revenues in H1 2027 versus 45% in prior years; management said it is too early to call further upside for H2 because it cannot yet tell whether demand holds at historically high prices and supply is unstable, and no additional pull-forwards are built into the forecast even though it projects further price increases this year. Hyperscale product revenue is expected to rise significantly in Q3 and Q4 based on customer order commitments agreed before the fiscal year began, and FY2027 hyperscaler revenue is expected to be a multiple of fiscal 2026's.
quarterly_data.figure: 48% of FY2027 revenue in H1 (vs 45% prior years); FY2027 hyperscaler revenue a multiple of fiscal 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Hyperscale business: Q1 hyperscale revenue contribution was minimal and the significant majority of hyperscaler revenue is expected in H2 FY2027, at 75%-85% gross margins that should lift aggregate product gross margin. The company is investing significant resources in system qualification with multiple prospects and expects to significantly expand hyperscale product shipments in the second half and even further next year. Q1 capital investments of $68 million (approximately 6.5% of revenue) supported scaling the hyperscale business as it ramps investments to qualify more NAND for hyperscalers, tech titans and cloud providers.
quarterly_data.figure: hyperscaler gross margins 75%-85%; Q1 capex $68 million (approximately 6.5% of revenue)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO on the NAND/memory supply crisis ('never seen another supply chain situation remotely like this'): prices have gone up 5x-10x on the spot market, long-term contracts at former prices 'were not worth the paper they were written on', quotes now come with at best 30 days of longevity and prices are 'doubling every 18 days'. He expects continued price increases at least through the summer, said capacity has been sold out through 2027 with interest in long-term contracts into 2028, and that fab capacity across NAND, memory, CPUs and now low-end chips is sold out. Everpure cut its customer quote validity from the 90-day quote it used for 15 years to a 30-day price quote.
quarterly_data.figure: spot prices up 5x-10x; capacity sold out through 2027; quote validity cut from 90-day to 30-day

quarterly_data.signal: CEO said hyperscalers are 'effectively desperate for storage capacity of any type in any form', which has increased the urgency of DirectFlash qualification; the solution replaces both SSDs and hard disk, and hard disk has been sold out through 2028. Qualification still has to be completed and how much NAND is actually available to Everpure remains a question — 'we could probably sell every terabyte of NAND that we could source.'

Product gross margin was 65.5%, at the low end of the 65%-70% long-term range, down 180 basis points sequentially mainly on increased commodities cost, partly offset by price increases and mix shift to higher-performance FlashArray and FlashBlade. Management is deliberately holding price increases later and lower than competitors and expects gradual product gross margin recovery in H2 as pricing catches up with rapidly rising input costs.
quarterly_data.figure: product gross margin 65.5%, down 180 basis points sequentially

quarterly_data.signal: AI storage: FlashBlade//EXA scored more wins including AI/ML and GPU-accelerated trading applications, with active discussions with dozens of prospective customers across the AI ecosystem; the company says it is beginning to displace competitive AI storage products in the enterprise and neo cloud markets. The CTO said longer inference context windows drive more demand for GPU-server memory, remote memory and remote storage, a large part of its partnership with NVIDIA around KV caching.

Storage-as-a-service momentum in the price spike: Evergreen//One sales were up 73% year-on-year and storage-as-a-service TCV grew to $165 million, as Evergreen//One saw significantly lower price increases than traditional product sales.
